question: A shopkeeper earns a profit of 26% on the cost price of an article after giving two successive discounts of 20% and 30% on the marked price to a customer. What would have been the profit percentage, had the shopkeeper given 26% discount only?
solution:
Given: 

A shopkeeper earns a profit of 26% on the cost price of an article after giving two successive discounts of 20% and 30%.

Concept used:

Successive discount of A% and B% results into

⇒ (A + B - {AB over 100})%

Selling Price = Cost Price + Cost Price × Profit%

Selling price = Marked Price - Marked Price × Discount%

Calculation:

Resultant discount after giving two successive discounts of 20% and 30%

⇒ (20 + 30 - {30 × 20} over 100)%

⇒ 44%
